parts.article:
Looking at daily life in ancient Rome
 
In this preface to a history, the writer explains the factors affecting the scope of his study.
 
A If our ideas on Roman life are not to become lost in confusion, we must study it within a strictly defined time. Nothing changes more rapidly than human customs. Looking at our own more familiar world, apart from the great scientific discoveries of recent centuries which have turned it upside down—steam, electricity, railways, motor cars and aeroplanes, for example—it is clear that the elementary forms of everyday life have been subject to increasing change. Potatoes, for example, were not introduced into Europe until the sixteenth century, coffee was first drunk there in the late sixteenth or early seventeenth, and the banana was used in desserts in Europe at the beginning of the twentieth. The law of change was not less operative in antiquity. It was a commonplace of Roman rhetoric to contrast the crude simplicity of the Republic (509BC–27BC) with the luxury and refinement of the imperial times which followed. There is no common measure, whether of home, or house, or furniture, between ages which are so different.
 
B Since a choice of time must necessarily be made, this history will confine itself to studying the generation which was born about the middle of the first century AD, toward the end of the reign of Claudius (41–54AD) or the beginning of the reign of Nero (54–68AD), and which lived on into the reign of Trajan (98–117AD) or of Hadrian (117–138AD). This generation saw the Roman Empire at its most powerful and prosperous. It was witness to the last conquests of the Caesars: the conquest of Dacia, in modern-day eastern Europe, which brought vast mineral wealth into the Empire, and the conquest of Arabia, which helped to bring the riches of India and East Asia flooding into Rome. In the material domain, this generation attained the pinnacle of ancient civilisation.
 
C By a fortunate coincidence—all the more fortunate in that Latin literature was soon to run nearly dry—this generation is the one whose records combine to offer us the most complete picture of Roman life that we possess. We have a profusion of vivid and picturesque descriptions, precise and colourful, in such works as the Epigrams of Martial, the Satires of Juvenal and the Letters of Pliny. In addition, the Forum of Trajan in Rome itself and the ruins of Herculaneum and Pompeii, the two prosperous resorts buried by the eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79AD, supply an immense fund of archaeological evidence. Later excavations have also restored to us the ruins of the city of Ostia, which date in the main from the time when the Emperor Hadrian created this great commercial city as a realisation of his town planning ideas. Fortune has favoured the historian of this time.
 
D It is not enough to focus our study of Roman life only on a fixed time. It would lack foundation and consistency if we did not also focus it in space—in the country or in the town. Even today when the facilities for communication bring something of the city into the smallest and most isolated country cottage, there remains a significant difference between rural existence and the excitement of city life: a much greater gulf separated the peasant from the townsman of antiquity. So large was the inequality between them that, according to the historian Rostovtzeff, it pitted one against the other in a fierce and silent struggle which pierced the wall protecting the Roman privileged classes from the barbarian flood from the north. When the barbarian forces began to invade Roman territory, the peasants decided to fight alongside them.
 
E The townsman, in fact, enjoyed all the goods and resources of the earth. The peasant knew nothing but unending labour without profit, and was unable to enjoy the activities available in even the poorest of cities: the liveliness of the sports field, the warmth of the public baths and the magnificence of public spectacles. In a work on the history of everyday life, we must give up any attempt to blend two such dissimilar pictures into one, and must choose between them. The time which we have chosen to describe day by day is that of those Roman subjects who spent their time exclusively in the town, or rather in The City, Rome, which they regarded as the hub and centre of the universe, proud and wealthy ruler of a world which seemed at that time to have been pacified for ever.
 
F To perform our task well, we must first try to form an adequate picture of the surroundings in which our subjects lived, and by which their lives were coloured, freeing ourselves from any misconceptions concerning it. We must seek to reconstruct the physical nature of the great city and the social milieu of the various classes of the hierarchy by which it was governed. We must also investigate the moral background of thought and sentiment which can help explain both its strength and its weaknesses. The way in which the Romans of Rome employed their time can only be studied satisfactorily after we have plotted out the main lines of the framework within which they lived and outside of which the routine of their daily life would be more or less unintelligible.

questions.question: What does the writer say about the period mentioned in the second paragraph?

analyses.content: A（移民）文中指财富流入（riches flooding in），非大规模移民���B（出口矿产）文中指征服达契亚带来了矿产（brought in），是获取而非出口；C（派军队控制贸易）文中指征服阿拉伯帮助带来了财富，未提及控制贸易。
(Paragraph B) “In the material domain, this generation attained the pinnacle of ancient civilisation.”

题目问作者对第二段提到的时期有何评价。原文B段末尾提到：“In the material domain, this generation attained the pinnacle of ancient civilisation（在物质领域，这一代人达到了古代文明的顶峰）”，物质领域的顶峰对应生活水平（standard of living）达到最高点，选 D (The Roman standard of living reached its highest level)。

analyses.content: 题目问奥斯提亚（Ostia）被提到是作为什么？原文C段提到后来的挖掘（Later excavations）向我们展示了奥斯提亚城的遗迹，这与庞贝等一起提供了“immense fund of archaeological evidence（巨大的考古证据资金/来源）”，选 B (an important area for archaeological research)。
A（文学）奥斯提亚是遗迹，文学证据是前文提到的Martial等人的作品；C（出生地）文中说是哈德良皇帝建造的（created），非出生地；D（布局相似）文中说是哈德良城市规划思想的实现，未提与罗马相似。
(Paragraph C) “Later excavations have also restored to us the ruins of the city of Ostia...”

analyses.content: 题目问“命运眷顾了这一时期的历史学家”这句话指的是什么？原文C段开头提到这是一个幸运的巧合（fortunate coincidence），因为这一代人的记录结合起来提供了“most complete picture（最完整的画面）”，拥有大量的文学描写和考古证据，即资料来源广泛，选 C (a wide range of sources is available for this period)。
这里的“Fortune”指史料留存的运气，而非历史学家的财富（A）或作品受欢迎程度（B）。
(Paragraph C) “...this generation is the one whose records combine to offer us the most complete picture of Roman life that we possess.”

questions.question: In comparing urban and rural life in the Roman Empire, the writer states that

analyses.content: (Paragraph D) “...a much greater gulf separated the peasant from the townsman of antiquity.”
题目问在比较罗马帝国的城乡生活时，作者指出了什么？原文D段提到在古代，农民与市民之间隔着“much greater gulf（更大的鸿沟）”，且这种不平等导致了激烈的斗争，说明两者几乎没有共同点，选 B (rural life and urban life had little in common)。
A（文盲）未提及；C（信息少）未提及；D（读者兴趣）未提及。重点在于强调巨大的“gulf（鸿沟）”和“inequality（不平等）”。

questions.question: Rome's conquest of Arabia resulted in large‑scale immigration from the east into Rome.

analyses.content: 题目说罗马征服阿拉伯导致了来自东方的大规模移民（large-scale immigration）进入罗马。原文B段只说征服阿拉伯帮助带来了“riches of India and East Asia flooding into Rome（印度和东亚的财富涌入罗马）”，是财富而非人口，文中未提及移民，选 NOT GIVEN。
“Riches flooding in” 不等于 “Immigration”。
(Paragraph B) “...conquest of Arabia, which helped to bring the riches of India and East Asia flooding into Rome.”

questions.question: More can be learned about Roman life from the literature of the period studied in this book than from later Latin literature.

analyses.content: 题目说从本书研究时期的文学中能学到的罗马生活比从**后期的拉丁文学（later Latin literature）**中更多。原文C段提到拉丁文学“was soon to run nearly dry（很快就要枯竭了）”，暗示后期文学资源贫乏，而该时期提供了最完整的画面，选 YES。
“Run nearly dry” 对应后期文学更少，支持了题目中的比较。
(Paragraph C) “...all the more fortunate in that Latin literature was soon to run nearly dry...”

questions.question: Discoveries at Herculaneum and Pompeii showed that certain beliefs about Roman life were wrong.

analyses.content: 题目说赫库兰尼姆和庞贝的发现表明关于罗马生活的某些信仰是错误的（beliefs... were wrong）。原文C段只说它们提供了“immense fund of archaeological evidence（巨大的考古证据）”，并未提及是否纠正了错误的信仰，选 NOT GIVEN。
原文只提到了证据的丰富性，没提对错。
(Paragraph C) “...supply an immense fund of archaeological evidence.”

questions.question: Roman peasants provided assistance to the Empire when it was attacked.

analyses.content: “Fight alongside them” 中的 them 指代 “barbarian forces”，意味着背叛了帝国。
(Paragraph D) “When the barbarian forces began to invade Roman territory, the peasants decided to fight alongside them.”
题目说当帝国受到攻击时，罗马农民提供了帮助（provided assistance）。原文D段末尾说当野蛮人入侵时，农民决定“fight alongside them（与他们[野蛮人]并肩作战）”，即帮助入侵者而非帝国，选 NO。

questions.question: Rural inhabitants of the Roman Empire had a difficult life.

analyses.content: 题目说罗马帝国的农村居民生活艰难（difficult life）。原文E段提到农民除了“unending labour without profit（无休止的劳动且没有利润）”外一无所知，这显然是艰难的生活，选 YES。
“Unending labour without profit” 对应 “difficult life”。
(Paragraph E) “The peasant knew nothing but unending labour without profit...”

questions.question: Entertainment facilities were limited to the city of Rome itself.

analyses.content: 题目说娱乐设施**仅限于（limited to）**罗马城本身。原文E段提到农民甚至无法享受“available in even the poorest of cities（即使在最贫穷的城市也有的）”活动，说明娱乐设施在其他城市也有，不限于罗马，选 NO。
“Available in even the poorest of cities” 否定了 “Limited to the city of Rome”。
(Paragraph E) “...unable to enjoy the activities available in even the poorest of cities...”

groups.contentHtml:
The scope of the writer's study

It was important for the writer to limit several aspects of his . He decided to focus on a limited in Roman history, and to concentrate on the section of the population who were . The writer was interested in the physical environment, the people that ruled the country and the that contributed both to Rome's strength and to its weaknesses.

analyses.content: (Paragraph A) “we must study it...”; (Paragraph F) “To perform our task well... investigate...”
题目说限制他的____的几个方面很重要。原文F段开头提到为了“perform our task well... investigate（执行好我们的任务……调查）”，且全文都在界定研究（study）的范围。选项中 investigation（调查/研究）最符合语境，对应study/task。
题目标题是 “The scope of the writer's study”，文中多处用 “study/investigate”。
题目说他决定专注于罗马历史上一个有限的____。原文B段开头提到“Since a choice of time must necessarily be made... confine itself to studying the generation（既然必须做出时间的选择……限制于研究这一代人）”，对应有限的时期，选 H (period)。
“Time / generation” 对应 “period”。
(Paragraph B) “Since a choice of time must necessarily be made...”
题目说专注于____的那部分人口。原文E段提到作者选择了那些“spent their time exclusively in the town（时间完全花在城镇里）”的罗马臣民，即市民，选 E (city-dwellers)。
“Spent time in town” 对应 “city-dwellers”。
(Paragraph E) “...Roman subjects who spent their time exclusively in the town...”
题目说作者对物理环境、统治者以及导致罗马强弱的____感兴趣。原文F段提到必须调查“moral background of thought and sentiment（思想和情感的道德背景）”，这可以解释其优势和劣势。道德背景、思想情感对应价值观，选 C (values)。
“Moral background of thought and sentiment” 概括为 “values”。
(Paragraph F) “We must also investigate the moral background of thought and sentiment which can help explain both its strength and its weaknesses.”
